topic: Wireframes and information architecture; navigation structures
title: A navigation map for the results app
instructions:
## Every screen reachable in three taps

A mobile app lets students check exam results. Screens: **Login**, **Home**, **Results** (list by semester), **Result detail**, **Transcript request**, **Profile**, **Help**. Rules from the design review:

- From Home a student reaches Results, Transcript request, Profile and Help directly.
- Result detail is reached only from Results, and goes back to Results.
- Transcript request returns to Home when submitted; the user must **confirm** before submitting (a decision).
- Help is reachable from every main screen (Home, Results, Profile).
- Login leads to Home; Profile has a **Log out** that returns to Login.

## Do this

Write the navigation flow with one node per screen and labelled flows for the actions (`Home -->|tap Results| Results`). Use a decision node for the confirmation.
hints: Results -->|tap a result| Detail[Result detail] and Detail -->|back| Results.
Transcript[Transcript request] -->|submit| Confirm{Confirm?} then Confirm -->|yes| Home and Confirm -->|no| Transcript.
Help needs flows from Home, Results and Profile; Profile -->|log out| Login.

checks.label: Transcript request leads back to Home

realityNote: Navigation maps are the cheapest usability test there is: count the taps to each goal and look for dead ends before any pixel is drawn. Mobile platforms add the system back button, which must behave consistently with the map.
